title: Annotatio III §.VII: Mid-XII — Transsubstantiation’s name invented (Peter of Blois / Stephen of Autun)
pass_a_gloss: For then, namely in the middle of the twelfth Century, through Peter of Blois Epistle 140, according to Cave p. 471, according to others through Stephen Bishop of Autun (Æduensis / Augustodunensis), On the Sacrament of the Altar in the Bibliotheca Patrum (whose author’s age and writings are nonetheless very uncertain), the name of Transsubstantiation was invented.
pass_b_english: Mid-twelfth century: the name Transsubstantiation is invented.
Cave points to Peter of Blois Ep. 140; others to Stephen of Autun On the Sacrament of the Altar (Bibliotheca Patrum — author and date very uncertain).
source_text: Nam tum, Seculo nempe XII. medio, per Petrum Blesensem Epistola 140, juxta Caveum p. 471, juxta alios per Stephanum Æduensem vel Augustodunensem Episcopum, de Sacramento Altaris in Bibliotheca Patrum (cujus tamen Autoris & ætas & scripta valdè incerta sunt) Transsubstantiationis nomen adinventum.
